name: NCERT-RAG-Eval
description: Abstract LLM-based tutoring systems risk producing wrong or hallucinated explanations unless grounded in trusted educational material. We propose NCERT-RAG-Eval, a curriculum-aligned benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) against official NCERT textbooks, the most widely used books in Indian STEM education. The framework indexes a 237-chunk NCERT corpus spanning five chapters and compares lexical (BM25), dense semantic (FAISS, ), and hybrid (reciprocal rank fusion) retrieval on recall, precision, and faithfulness. On 88 gold-annotated questions spanning motion, light, electricity, and magnetic effects, hybrid retrieval performs best (Recall 0.818, Precision 0.348), closely followed by FAISS (0.807, 0.341) and clearly ahead of BM25 (0.682, 0.280); on a paraphrased subset, Hybrid shows no Recall drop at all, while FAISS drops the most. Growing the corpus with non-duplicated distractor content leaves Precision essentially flat even at more than four times the original corpus size, unlike the sharp degradation seen under duplication-based growth.
